market.title: EU Parliament Approves PSD3, Mandating Instant Payments
market.summary_short: The European Parliament has officially approved PSD3, marking a significant regulatory update for payment services. This new directive aims to enhance consumer protection, combat fraud, and make instant payments the default for most transactions.
market.summary_detail: The European Parliament's recent approval of PSD3 is set to transform the European payment landscape. A key provision mandates that instant payments become the standard for credit transfers, significantly reducing processing times and increasing liquidity for businesses. The directive also introduces stricter requirements for fraud prevention, including enhanced authentication measures and improved information sharing among payment service providers. Furthermore, PSD3 emphasizes greater transparency for consumers and aims to foster further innovation in Open Banking by refining API standards. This legislative move is expected to drive significant changes in payment infrastructure and operational processes across the EU and EEA, with a phased implementation timeline stretching into 2027.
key_points: PSD3 officially approved by European Parliament.
Mandatory instant payments for most credit transfers.
Enhanced fraud prevention measures and data sharing.
Refined Open Banking API standards for innovation.
market.rbi_cash_management: RBI Cash Management and its CMIplus platform must ensure full compliance with PSD3 mandates, particularly regarding instant payment processing and enhanced fraud prevention. This presents an opportunity to strengthen CMIplus's real-time payment capabilities and offer advanced security features to corporate clients in CEE.

market.title: CEE Corporates Accelerate ISO 20022 Migration for Treasury Systems
market.summary_short: Corporates in Central and Eastern Europe are rapidly advancing their migration to the ISO 20022 standard, driven by regulatory deadlines and the desire for enhanced data capabilities. This shift impacts treasury systems and payment processing across the region.
market.summary_detail: The adoption of ISO 20022 is gaining significant momentum among CEE corporates, moving beyond mere compliance to strategic advantage. Companies are leveraging the richer data capabilities of ISO 20022 to improve reconciliation, automate treasury processes, and gain deeper insights into their cash flows. This acceleration is particularly visible in countries aligning with broader European payment infrastructure upgrades. Many are upgrading their ERP and TMS systems to fully support the standard, often integrating via channels like EBICS v3.2 or H2H connections. The transition, while complex, promises greater efficiency, reduced manual effort, and better interoperability for multi-currency payments across diverse banking networks.

Richer data improves reconciliation and treasury automation.
Upgrades to ERP/TMS systems are critical for full adoption.
EBICS v3.2 and H2H are key integration channels.

market.title: AI-Powered Fraud Prevention Becomes Essential for Real-Time Payments
market.summary_short: With the increasing prevalence of instant payments, AI and machine learning are becoming indispensable for effective fraud detection and prevention. Financial institutions and corporates are investing in advanced solutions to combat sophisticated fraud schemes.
market.summary_detail: The shift towards real-time payments, while offering immense benefits, also presents new challenges for fraud prevention. The speed of transactions leaves little room for traditional manual checks, making AI and machine learning crucial for identifying suspicious patterns instantly. Solutions leveraging AI can analyze vast datasets, detect anomalies, and flag potential fraud in milliseconds, significantly reducing financial losses. Furthermore, the importance of Payment Order Verification (VoP) services is growing, as they provide an additional layer of security by verifying beneficiary details before a payment is executed. Corporates are increasingly seeking integrated fraud prevention tools within their cash management platforms to protect against evolving cyber threats and payment fraud typologies.

AI analyzes vast data to identify suspicious transaction patterns.
Payment Order Verification (VoP) adds critical security layer.
Corporates seek integrated fraud prevention within platforms.

Banks need to prepare for increased real-time liquidity demands and adjust their treasury operations to comply with the new requirements and leverage the opportunities presented by these regulatory changes. regulatory.title: EBA Updates Fraud Taxonomy to Version 7.0, Effective January 2027
regulatory.summary_short: The EBA has released version 7.0 of its Fraud Taxonomy, effective 1 January 2027, updating classifications to reflect latest fraud trends. This taxonomy will support harmonised pan-European fraud-fighting and data sharing under the forthcoming Payment Services Regulation.
regulatory.summary_detail: The Euro Banking Association (EBA) has published version 7.0 of its EBA Fraud Taxonomy, which will become effective on 1 January 2027. This annual review, supported by fraud experts, ensures the taxonomy remains relevant to evolving fraud trends. Key updates in version 7.0 include replacing 'emotional manipulation' with more specific modi like 'support a friend or family member fraud', 'romance fraud', and 'charity / donation fraud'. Additionally, new labels have been added for suspected money mule activity and 'card chip relay' fraud. The taxonomy provides a standardised framework for describing and categorising payment fraud scenarios, improving data comparability, monitoring, reporting, and information sharing, particularly in anticipation of the forthcoming Payment Services Regulation (PSR), which is part of the PSD3 package.
key_points: EBA Fraud Taxonomy version 7.0 takes effect on 1 January 2027.
Updates include more specific classifications for 'emotional manipulation' fraud types.
New labels added for money mule activity and 'card chip relay' fraud.
Aims to harmonise fraud data and support information sharing under the new PSR/PSD3.
regulatory.rbi_cash_management: RBI Cash Management (CMIplus) must review and integrate EBA Fraud Taxonomy version 7.0 into its fraud monitoring and reporting systems by January 2027. This ensures compliance with updated classification standards and prepares for future data sharing requirements under the Payment Services Regulation, enhancing fraud detection for CEE operations.
